```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


Your document must be knit-able to Word, PDF, or HTML, and output must contain at least the following elements:

    A graph showing the IQ levels by location status
    At least one nicely formatted table (hint: try the 'kable' function in the knitr R package or one of the popular table R packages like tableone, table1, or gtsummary)
    A couple sentences of text (not on the graph, but in the body of the R Markdown document) describing the graph and the table
    In-line calculations giving the values of the means, that will be updated if the data are changed (hint: use syntax `r `)
    At least one R code chunk.



## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
